"""Export: renders every segment in parallel (unchanged segments are reused), assembles cuts and transitions,
burns in the type, lays the soundtrack under it, and writes the deliverables: the video, a poster, the edit
decision list (CMX 3600, opens in Premiere / Resolve) and the edit as JSON."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from ... import media
from ..model import AgentRun
from ..render import render_segment
from .base import Agent, Ctx, fps_arg, frame_size, out_fps

XFADE = {"whip": "slideleft", "dissolve": "fade", "flash": "fadewhite"}


def _tc(t: float, fps: float) -> str:
    f = int(round(fps))
    n = int(round(t * fps))
    return f"{n // (3600 * f):02d}:{n // (60 * f) % 60:02d}:{n // f % 60:02d}:{n % f:02d}"


def edl(ctx: Ctx, fps: float) -> str:
    p = ctx.project
    lines = [f"TITLE: {p.name}", "FCM: NON-DROP FRAME", ""]
    n = 0
    for g in p.timeline:
        if g.kind != "clip":
            continue
        n += 1
        c = p.clip(g.clip)
        reel = c.id.upper()[:8]
        lines.append(f"{n:03d}  {reel:<8} V     C        {_tc(g.src_in, fps)} {_tc(g.src_out, fps)} "
                     f"{_tc(g.start, fps)} {_tc(g.start + g.length, fps)}")
        lines.append(f"* FROM CLIP NAME: {c.name}")
        if abs(g.speed - 1) > 1e-3:
            lines.append(f"M2   {reel:<8}      {g.speed * fps:05.1f}                {_tc(g.src_in, fps)}")
        if g.trans != "cut":
            lines.append(f"* TRANSITION: {g.trans} {g.trans_d:.2f}s")
        lines.append(f"* {g.role.upper()}: {g.why}")
        lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


class Export(Agent):
    key, title, icon, color = "export", "Export", "export", "#7dcfff"
    role = "renders every segment in parallel, assembles cuts and transitions, burns in the type, lays in the sound"
    needs = ("colorist", "typographer", "mixer")

    def inputs(self, ctx: Ctx):
        p = ctx.project
        return [p.timeline and [g.model_dump(exclude={"thumb", "why", "score"}) for g in p.timeline], p.look.get("luts"),
                p.look.get("fx"), p.look.get("grain"), ctx.skill.get("motion"), ctx.settings.aspect, ctx.settings.resolution,
                out_fps(p), (ctx.root / "render" / "text.ass").read_text(encoding="utf-8") if (ctx.root / "render" / "text.ass").exists() else "",
                p.audio.file, p.audio.model_dump()]

    def run(self, ctx: Ctx, rep: AgentRun) -> None:
        p, s = ctx.project, ctx.settings
        W, H = frame_size(s)
        fps = out_fps(p)
        fx, grain = dict(p.look.get("fx") or {}), p.look.get("grain")
        letterbox = fx.pop("letterbox", None)
        M = dict(ctx.skill.get("motion") or {})
        segdir = ctx.root / "render" / "segs"
        segdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        tl = p.timeline
        jobs = []
        for i, g in enumerate(tl):
            lut = p.look.get("luts", {}).get(g.clip) if g.kind == "clip" else None
            whip_in = g.trans_d / 2 + 0.03 if g.trans == "whip" else 0.0
            nxt = tl[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(tl) else None
            whip_out = nxt.trans_d / 2 + 0.03 if nxt is not None and nxt.trans == "whip" else 0.0
            key = hashlib.sha1(json.dumps([g.model_dump(exclude={"thumb", "why", "score", "start", "id", "role"}),
                                           p.clip(g.clip).master if g.kind == "clip" else "", lut, fx, grain, W, H, fps,
                                           {k: M.get(k) for k in ("cadence", "weave")}, whip_in, whip_out, "v1"],
                                          sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:14]
            jobs.append((g, lut, whip_in, whip_out, segdir / f"{key}.mp4"))
        todo = [j for j in jobs if not j[4].exists()]
        self.say(ctx, f"rendering {len(todo)} of {len(jobs)} segments ({len(jobs) - len(todo)} unchanged, reused)")

        def one(job):
            g, lut, wi, wo, out = job
            tmp = out.with_suffix(".tmp.mp4")
            render_segment(ctx, g, p.clip(g.clip) if g.kind == "clip" else None, W, H, fps, lut, fx, grain,
                           M, tmp, wi, wo)
            tmp.replace(out)
            return g.id

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(3) as ex:
            for sid in ex.map(one, todo):
                self.say(ctx, f"segment {sid} rendered", kind="progress", seg=sid)
        # assemble
        inputs, graph = [], []
        for i, (g, *_rest, out) in enumerate(jobs):
            inputs += ["-i", ctx.rel(out)]
            graph.append(f"[{i}:v]settb=AVTB,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,fps={fps_arg(fps)},format=yuv420p[s{i}]")
        acc, acc_d = "s0", tl[0].length
        for i in range(1, len(tl)):
            g = tl[i]
            if g.trans != "cut" and g.trans_d > 0:
                graph.append(f"[{acc}][s{i}]xfade=transition={XFADE.get(g.trans, 'fade')}:duration={g.trans_d:.4f}:"
                             f"offset={max(acc_d - g.trans_d, 0):.4f}[x{i}]")
                acc_d += g.length - g.trans_d
            else:
                graph.append(f"[{acc}][s{i}]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0[x{i}]")
                acc_d += g.length
            acc = f"x{i}"
        post = []
        if letterbox and W > H:
            bar = max(0, int(round((H - W / float(letterbox)) / 2)))
            if bar:
                post.append(f"drawbox=x=0:y=0:w=iw:h={bar}:color=black:t=fill,drawbox=x=0:y=ih-{bar}:w=iw:h={bar}:color=black:t=fill")
        if p.texts and (ctx.root / "render" / "text.ass").exists():
            post.append("subtitles=render/text.ass:fontsdir=render/fonts")
        post.append("format=yuv420p")
        graph.append(f"[{acc}]{','.join(post)}[vout]")
        audio_i = len(jobs)
        inputs += ["-i", p.audio.file]
        final = ctx.root / "final.mp4"
        tmp = ctx.root / "final.tmp.mp4"
        T = p.duration
        ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", *inputs, "-filter_complex", ";".join(graph), "-map", "[vout]", "-map", f"{audio_i}:a",
                    "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "18", "-profile:v", "high", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
                    "-color_primaries", "bt709", "-color_trc", "bt709", "-colorspace", "bt709", "-r", fps_arg(fps),
                    "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "256k", "-ar", "48000", "-t", f"{T:.4f}", "-movflags", "+faststart",
                    ctx.rel(tmp)], timeout=3600)
        tmp.replace(final)
        # thumbnails for the timeline + poster
        thumbs = ctx.root / "render" / "thumbs"
        thumbs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for f in thumbs.glob("t_*.jpg"):
            f.unlink()
        frames = [max(0, int(round((g.start + g.length / 2) * fps))) for g in tl]
        sel = "+".join(f"eq(n,{n})" for n in sorted(set(frames)))
        ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", "-i", "final.mp4", "-vf", f"select='{sel}',scale=-2:160", "-fps_mode", "passthrough",
                    "-q:v", "4", "render/thumbs/t_%03d.jpg"])
        order = sorted(set(frames))
        for g, n in zip(tl, frames):
            g.thumb = f"render/thumbs/t_{order.index(n) + 1:03d}.jpg"
        story = next((t for t in p.texts if t.kind in ("story", "stamp")), None)
        pt = (story.start + story.end) / 2 if story else next((g.start + g.length / 2 for g in tl if g.kind == "clip"), 0)
        media.frame(final, pt, ctx.root / "poster.jpg", height=720)
        (ctx.root / "edit.edl").write_text(edl(ctx, fps), encoding="utf-8")
        (ctx.root / "edit.json").write_text(json.dumps({"timeline": [g.model_dump() for g in tl],
                                                        "texts": [t.model_dump() for t in p.texts],
                                                        "audio": p.audio.model_dump(), "look": {k: v for k, v in p.look.items() if k != "graded"},
                                                        "credit": p.track.credit if p.track else None}, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
        size = final.stat().st_size
        p.outputs = {"video": "final.mp4", "poster": "poster.jpg", "edl": "edit.edl", "json": "edit.json",
                     "bytes": size, "width": W, "height": H, "fps": fps, "duration": T,
                     "credit": p.track.credit if p.track else ""}
        self.decide(ctx, rep, f"final.mp4: {W}x{H} {fps:g} fps, {T:.1f}s, {size / 1e6:.1f} MB (H.264 + AAC, Rec.709)")
        self.decide(ctx, rep, f"{len(todo)} segment(s) rendered, {len(jobs) - len(todo)} reused · edit list for Premiere/Resolve: edit.edl")
        rep.preview = "poster.jpg"
        rep.summary = f"{W}x{H} · {T:.1f}s · {len(todo)}/{len(jobs)} rendered"

"""QA: measures the finished video and sends failures back to the agent responsible.

Every check is a measurement of the rendered file (or the edit that made it): duration, format, black and
frozen frames that weren't intended, loudness and true peak, pacing against the skill, cuts on the beat,
colour distance from the reference. A failure names its owner and a fix; the line re-runs from that agent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from ... import media
from .. import analysis as an
from .. import look
from ..model import AgentRun
from .base import Agent, Ctx, frame_size, out_fps


class QA(Agent):
    key, title, icon, color = "qa", "QA", "shield", "#41a6b5"
    role = "measures the finished video and sends any failure back to the agent responsible"
    needs = ("export",)

    def inputs(self, ctx: Ctx):
        return [ctx.project.outputs.get("bytes"), ctx.project.outputs.get("duration")]

    def run(self, ctx: Ctx, rep: AgentRun) -> None:
        p, s = ctx.project, ctx.settings
        final = ctx.root / "final.mp4"
        info = media.probe(final)
        W, H = frame_size(s)
        fps = out_fps(p)
        T = p.duration
        self.check(ctx, rep, "render complete", abs(info["duration"] - T) <= 2.5 / fps + 0.05 and info["has_audio"],
                   f"{info['duration']:.2f}s vs {T:.2f}s planned, audio {'yes' if info['has_audio'] else 'missing'}",
                   owner="export")
        self.check(ctx, rep, "format", (info["width"], info["height"]) == (W, H), f"{info['width']}x{info['height']}",
                   owner="export")
        if s.length:
            self.check(ctx, rep, "length", abs(T - s.length) <= max(1.0, 0.06 * s.length),
                       f"{T:.1f}s for a {s.length:.0f}s target", owner="cutter",
                       hint={"length_scale": round(s.length / max(T, 0.1), 3)})
        # intended black: cards and fades
        planned = [(g.start, g.start + g.length) for g in p.timeline if g.kind == "card"]
        planned += [(g.start, g.start + g.fade_in + 0.15) for g in p.timeline if g.fade_in]
        planned += [(g.start + g.length - g.fade_out - 0.15, g.start + g.length) for g in p.timeline if g.fade_out]

        def intended(a: float, b: float) -> bool:
            return any(a >= x - 0.12 and b <= y + 0.12 for x, y in planned)

        blacks = [(a, b) for a, b in media.black_frames(final, 0.25) if not intended(a, b)]
        avoid = []
        for a, b in blacks:
            for g in p.timeline:
                if g.kind == "clip" and g.start < b and a < g.start + g.length:
                    sa = g.src_in + max(a - g.start, 0) * g.speed
                    avoid.append([g.clip, round(sa, 2), round(sa + (b - a) * g.speed, 2)])
        self.check(ctx, rep, "no unintended black", not blacks,
                   "none" if not blacks else ", ".join(f"{a:.1f}–{b:.1f}s" for a, b in blacks[:3]),
                   owner="cutter", hint={"avoid": avoid})
        frozen = [t for t in media.frozen_frames(final, 1.2)
                  if not any(x - 0.1 <= t <= y for x, y in planned)]
        self.check(ctx, rep, "no frozen picture", not frozen, "none" if not frozen else ", ".join(f"{t:.1f}s" for t in frozen[:3]),
                   owner="cutter", hint={"length_scale": 0.92})
        loud = media.loudness(final)
        if loud:
            self.check(ctx, rep, "loudness", abs(loud["lufs"] - p.audio.lufs) <= 1.2 and loud["true_peak"] <= -0.3,
                       f"{loud['lufs']:.1f} LUFS (target {p.audio.lufs:g}), peak {loud['true_peak']:.1f} dBTP", owner="mixer")
        clips = [g for g in p.timeline if g.kind == "clip"]
        P = ctx.skill.get("pace") or {}
        if clips and not P.get("jumpcut"):
            holds = [g.length for g in clips if g.role != "burst"]
            target = float(P.get("shot", 2.5)) / max(s.pacing, 0.3)
            avg = float(np.mean(holds)) if holds else 0
            ok = 0.55 * target <= avg <= 1.8 * target
            self.check(ctx, rep, "pacing", ok, f"average hold {avg:.2f}s vs {target:.2f}s for {ctx.skill.get('label')}",
                       owner="cutter")
        if p.track and s.beat_sync and len(p.track.beats) > 8 and clips:
            bt = np.array(p.track.beats) - p.audio.music_in
            sub = np.sort(np.concatenate([bt, (bt[:-1] + bt[1:]) / 2]))
            cut_pts = [g.start + (g.trans_d / 2 if g.trans != "cut" else 0) for g in clips[1:]]
            on = sum(1 for c in cut_pts if np.min(np.abs(sub - c)) <= 1.0 / fps + 0.005)
            self.check(ctx, rep, "cuts on the beat", not cut_pts or on >= 0.85 * len(cut_pts),
                       f"{on}/{len(cut_pts)} cuts within a frame of a beat", owner="cutter")
        ref = p.reference
        if ref and ref.profile and s.match_reference and clips:
            fr = an.frames(final, 2.0, an.analysis_size(W, H, 160))
            keep = [i for i in range(len(fr)) if not any(x <= i / 2.0 <= y for x, y in planned)]
            if keep:
                px = look.pixel_sample(fr[keep])
                de = look.delta_e(look.stats(px)["lab_mean"], ref.profile["look"]["lab_mean"])
                self.check(ctx, rep, "colour matches the reference", de < 10,
                           f"ΔE {de:.1f} between the finished video and the reference (under 10 passes)",
                           owner="colorist", hint={"boost_ref": 0.15})
        failed = [c for c in rep.checks if not c["ok"]]
        p.qa = rep.checks
        rep.summary = "all checks pass" if not failed else f"{len(failed)} check(s) failed: " + ", ".join(c["name"] for c in failed)
        rep.preview = "poster.jpg"

def subject_track(fr: np.ndarray, chunk: int = 96) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Horizontal position of the main subject per frame (0..1) and a confidence.

    Combines spectral-residual saliency (Hou & Zhang 2007), motion that differs from the frame's typical
    motion (a moving subject rather than a moving camera) and skin tone, with a mild centre prior."""
    n = len(fr)
    xs_out, conf = np.zeros(n, np.float32), np.zeros(n, np.float32)
    prev = None
    for a in range(0, n, chunk):
        b = min(n, a + chunk)
        f = fr[a:b, ::2, ::2].astype(np.float32) / 255.0
        g = f @ LUMA
        F = np.fft.fft2(g)
        amp, ph = np.log(np.abs(F) + 1e-6), np.angle(F)
        sal = np.abs(np.fft.ifft2(np.exp((amp - blur2(amp, 1)) + 1j * ph))) ** 2
        sal = blur2(blur2(sal.astype(np.float32), 2), 2)
        sal /= sal.reshape(b - a, -1).max(1)[:, None, None] + 1e-9
        seq = g if prev is None else np.concatenate([prev[None], g])
        md = np.abs(np.diff(seq, axis=0)) if len(seq) > 1 else np.zeros((0, *g.shape[1:]), np.float32)
        if prev is None:
            md = np.concatenate([np.zeros((1, *g.shape[1:]), np.float32), md])
        md = np.clip(md - np.median(md.reshape(len(md), -1), 1)[:, None, None], 0, None)
        md = blur2(md, 2)
        md /= md.reshape(len(md), -1).max(1)[:, None, None] + 1e-6
        r, gg, bb = f[..., 0] * 255, f[..., 1] * 255, f[..., 2] * 255
        y = 0.299 * r + 0.587 * gg + 0.114 * bb
        cb = 128 - 0.168736 * r - 0.331264 * gg + 0.5 * bb
        cr = 128 + 0.5 * r - 0.418688 * gg - 0.081312 * bb
        skin = blur2(((cr > 136) & (cr < 173) & (cb > 77) & (cb < 125) & (y > 45)).astype(np.float32), 2)
        wmap = 0.5 * sal + 0.35 * md + 0.3 * skin
        xs = np.linspace(0, 1, g.shape[2], dtype=np.float32)
        wmap *= (0.55 + 0.45 * np.exp(-((xs - 0.5) ** 2) / (2 * 0.28 ** 2)))[None, None, :]
        col = wmap.sum(1) ** 2
        xs_out[a:b] = (col * xs).sum(1) / (col.sum(1) + 1e-9)
        conf[a:b] = col.max(1) / (col.mean(1) + 1e-9)
        prev = g[-1]
    return xs_out, conf

def _pnorm(m: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Normalise each frame of a map stack by its 99th percentile."""
    hi = np.percentile(m.reshape(len(m), -1), 99, axis=1)[:, None, None]
    return np.clip(m / (hi + 1e-6), 0, 1)


def subject_track(fr: np.ndarray, fps: float = 8.0) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Horizontal position of the main subject per frame (0..1) and a confidence. No model:

    - activity: where the picture changes over ~1.5 s, minus the frame's typical change (so a moving subject
      counts and a moving camera doesn't);
    - colour that stands out from the frame (opponent colour distance from the frame's mean);
    - skin tone, and spectral-residual saliency (Hou & Zhang 2007) as a weak prior.
    The position is the peak of the column profile, refined by a local centroid (an average over the whole
    frame would drift to the centre on textured scenes)."""
    n = len(fr)
    if n == 0:
        return np.zeros(0, np.float32), np.zeros(0, np.float32)
    f = fr[:, ::2, ::2].astype(np.float32) / 255.0
    g = f @ LUMA
    lag = max(1, int(round(fps * 0.25)))
    d = np.zeros_like(g)
    if n > lag:
        d[lag:] = np.abs(g[lag:] - g[:-lag])
        d[:lag] = d[lag]
    d = np.clip(d - np.median(d.reshape(n, -1), 1)[:, None, None], 0, None)
    act = box(d, max(1, int(fps * 0.75)), 0)  # accumulate over ~1.5 s
    act = _pnorm(blur2(act, 2))
    o1, o2 = f[..., 0] - f[..., 1], (f[..., 0] + f[..., 1]) / 2 - f[..., 2]
    col = np.sqrt((o1 - o1.mean((1, 2), keepdims=True)) ** 2 + (o2 - o2.mean((1, 2), keepdims=True)) ** 2)
    col = _pnorm(blur2(col, 2))
    r, gg, bb = f[..., 0] * 255, f[..., 1] * 255, f[..., 2] * 255
    y = 0.299 * r + 0.587 * gg + 0.114 * bb
    cb = 128 - 0.168736 * r - 0.331264 * gg + 0.5 * bb
    cr = 128 + 0.5 * r - 0.418688 * gg - 0.081312 * bb
    skin = blur2(((cr > 136) & (cr < 173) & (cb > 77) & (cb < 125) & (y > 45)).astype(np.float32), 2)
    sal = np.zeros_like(g)
    for a in range(0, n, 128):
        F = np.fft.fft2(g[a:a + 128])
        amp, ph = np.log(np.abs(F) + 1e-6), np.angle(F)
        sal[a:a + 128] = (np.abs(np.fft.ifft2(np.exp((amp - blur2(amp, 1)) + 1j * ph))) ** 2).astype(np.float32)
    sal = _pnorm(blur2(blur2(sal, 2), 2))
    has_act = (act.reshape(n, -1).mean(1) > 0.02)[:, None, None]
    wmap = np.where(has_act, 0.55 * act + 0.2 * col + 0.15 * skin + 0.1 * sal, 0.45 * col + 0.3 * skin + 0.25 * sal)
    w = g.shape[2]
    xs = np.linspace(0, 1, w, dtype=np.float32)
    prof = wmap.sum(1) * (0.8 + 0.2 * np.exp(-((xs - 0.5) ** 2) / (2 * 0.3 ** 2)))[None, :]
    prof = box(prof, max(1, w // 24), 1)
    peak = prof.argmax(1)
    span = max(2, int(w * 0.12))
    out = np.zeros(n, np.float32)
    for i in range(n):
        lo, hi = max(0, peak[i] - span), min(w, peak[i] + span + 1)
        p = prof[i, lo:hi] - prof[i].mean()
        p = np.clip(p, 0, None) + 1e-9
        out[i] = float((p * xs[lo:hi]).sum() / p.sum())
    conf = (prof.max(1) / (prof.mean(1) + 1e-9)).astype(np.float32)
    return out, conf

1	# Cutroom
2	
3	**An AI post-production team you can hand raw footage and a one-line brief, and walk away.**
4	A logger watches every clip, a producer writes the spec, an editor agent cuts it with real editing tools, a motion
5	designer makes the titles and thumbnail, and a critic watches every draft and sends it back until it's good enough to
6	post. Every render is measured (length, black and frozen frames, loudness, pacing, caption speed), every decision is
7	traced in [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com), and a crash resumes mid-edit.
8	
9	```
10	$ cutroom make "30s vertical teaser for Reels: open on the robot attack, best dialogue with captions, end on the title" \
11	    footage/tears-of-steel/*.mov
12	```
13	
14	Outputs: `final.mp4` (9:16, word-by-word captions, animated titles, loudness-normalised to −14 LUFS), `thumbnail.png`,
15	`captions.srt`, and an **edit sheet** (`index.html`): the cut list with a frame per segment, every quality check, and
16	the creative director's notes, round by round.
17	
18	> Built for #neatHack 2026 ("Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching"). Work in progress.
19	
20	## The team
21	
22	| Agent | What it decides | What keeps it honest |
23	|---|---|---|
24	| **Logger** | Watches each clip (Gemini video understanding on a 360p proxy) and logs it shot by shot: description, energy, quality, usefulness, highlights | Shot boundaries snapped to FFmpeg scene changes; words and timings come from Whisper, not from the model; if no vision model is available it logs from scene cuts + transcript and the edit continues |
25	| **Producer** | Platform, aspect ratio, target length, hook, structure, captions, titles, house style | Target length clamped to what the footage can actually fill |
26	| **Editor** (tool-calling loop) | Every cut: `list_shots`, `read_transcript`, `add_segment`, `trim_segment`, `move_segment`, `set_zoom`, `set_captions`, `add_title`, `preview`, `render_draft`, `finish` | Times must exist in the source; cuts that land mid-word are flagged with the nearest clean point; the running duration and pacing are shown after every action; `finish` is refused until the current timeline is rendered and its checks pass |
27	| **Motion designer** | Title cards, lower thirds, end cards, thumbnail | HTML/CSS templates rendered to transparent PNGs and animated by FFmpeg, in the house style |
28	| **Critic** | Watches the rendered draft like a creative director: hook, pacing, story, legibility, anything broken; approve or revise with up to 4 concrete fixes | Measurable checks run on every render; approval needs a score ≥ 7 |
29	
30	## Taste without fine-tuning: learn a creator's style from their public videos
31	
32	```
33	cutroom style learn --name bonzo --url https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sKdC4Bs-cKA --url https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tonG-OufefQ
34	```
35	
36	A vision model watches windows of the creator's **public** videos through Gemini's own YouTube-URL input (nothing is
37	downloaded or re-used) and reports, in a fixed structure: the time of every cut, every piece of on-screen text (words,
38	case, position, size, font feel), the look (temperature, contrast, saturation, black level, grain, vignette,
39	letterbox), camera, transitions and speed changes, sound (voice-over vs to-camera, music role, cuts on the beat), how
40	the video opens and is built, and its signature moves. Cutroom turns that into a **style profile** the renderer can
41	execute and the critic can measure against: shot rhythm, a concrete grade, the text treatment, the story structure.
42	
43	Profiles learned from the references this project was asked to edit like:
44	
45	| Profile | Learned signature |
46	|---|---|
47	| `bonzo` (@Wordisbonz, "turning my life into short movies") | the story told in bold lowercase text lines; time/place stamps; long handheld walk-and-talk takes with occasional whip-pan bursts; warm, soft, lightly grained look; centred serif title cards on black |
48	| `farza` (@farzatv) | direct-to-camera confessional; tight jump cuts that remove every pause inside a take; handheld selfie framing that drifts to B-roll; no text, no music |
49	| `mayv` (@mayv_music) | handheld roaming documentary; location stamps; phrase-by-phrase lowercase subtitles; rapid hard cuts on the beat in music sections |
50	
51	Only the style is learned. The editor writes its own lines about *your* footage; lines copied from the reference
52	creator are refused, and the raw observations (which quote the creators' on-screen text) stay out of the repo. Cut
53	timings come from a vision model sampling 3 frames a second, so rhythm is an estimate (two models disagreed by 3x on
54	one creator; the stronger model's reading is used).
55	
56	For local reference videos you have the right to analyse, `cutroom style learn <files> --name x` measures them
57	directly with FFmpeg instead (shot-length distribution, brightness/saturation, loudness, words per second).
58	
59	## What the editor can do
60	
61	Cuts and trims, **jump cuts that strip pauses out of talking footage** (alternating a subtle punch-in to hide them),
62	slow motion and speed changes, dip-to-black, punch-in zooms, **subject-aware reframing** to vertical, word-by-word or
63	minimal lowercase captions, **story text and time/place stamps**, title and end cards, music ducked under speech, and a
64	**film look** per style (colour temperature, lifted or crushed blacks, vignette, grain, letterbox). Flat/log footage gets
65	an automatic **primary colour correction** (levels stretch, mid-tone and saturation recovery) before the creative look,
66	and anything over 1080p is edited from an optimised 1080p master.
67	
68	## Demo footage
69	
70	The demos use Blender Foundation open movies (*Tears of Steel*, *Sintel*), CC BY 3.0. See `footage/README.md`.
71

"""Offline tests for the studio's algorithms (no network, no models).

Run: uv run python tests/test_studio.py
"""

import sys
import tempfile
import wave
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from cutroom.studio import analysis as an  # noqa: E402
from cutroom.studio import look  # noqa: E402
from cutroom.studio.agents.cutter import NEG, assign_story, plan_beats, plan_free  # noqa: E402
from cutroom.studio.agents.typographer import ass_document  # noqa: E402
from cutroom.studio.model import Text  # noqa: E402


def test_beat_tracker_finds_the_tempo():
    sr, bpm, secs = 22050, 100.0, 30
    y = np.zeros(sr * secs, np.float32)
    period = 60 / bpm
    for k in range(int(secs / period)):
        i = int(k * period * sr)
        n = np.arange(int(0.03 * sr))
        y[i:i + len(n)] += np.sin(2 * np.pi * 120 * n / sr) * np.exp(-n / (0.006 * sr)) * (1.0 if k % 4 == 0 else 0.6)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        path = Path(d) / "clicks.wav"
        with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as w:
            w.setnchannels(1)
            w.setsampwidth(2)
            w.setframerate(sr)
            w.writeframes((np.clip(y, -1, 1) * 32000).astype(np.int16).tobytes())
        m = an.analyse_music(path)
    assert abs(m["tempo"] - bpm) < 2.5, m["tempo"]
    gaps = np.diff(m["beats"])
    assert abs(np.median(gaps) - period) < 0.02 and len(m["beats"]) > 40


def test_primary_correction_rescues_flat_footage():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
    base = rng.uniform(0.2, 0.55, (20000, 1))
    px = np.clip(base + rng.normal(0, 0.01, (20000, 3)) + [0.01, 0.0, -0.01], 0, 1).astype(np.float32)
    p = look.primary_params(px)
    out = look.apply_primary(px, p)
    lum = look.luma(out)
    assert p["black"] > 0.1 and p["white"] < 0.7, p
    assert np.percentile(lum, 99) > 0.85 and np.percentile(lum, 1) < 0.1
    assert look.hsv_sat(out).mean() > look.hsv_sat(px).mean()


def test_normal_footage_is_left_alone():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
    px = rng.uniform(0, 1, (20000, 3)).astype(np.float32)
    p = look.primary_params(px)
    assert p["black"] == 0 and p["white"] == 1 and p["sat"] == 1.0


def test_reference_transfer_moves_colour_to_the_reference():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
    src_px = np.clip(rng.normal([0.3, 0.4, 0.6], 0.1, (20000, 3)), 0, 1).astype(np.float32)  # cool
    ref_px = np.clip(rng.normal([0.65, 0.45, 0.3], 0.12, (20000, 3)), 0, 1).astype(np.float32)  # warm
    s, r = look.stats(src_px), look.stats(ref_px)
    out = look.stats(look.transfer(src_px, s, r, 1.0))
    assert look.delta_e(out["lab_mean"], r["lab_mean"]) < look.delta_e(s["lab_mean"], r["lab_mean"]) / 4


def test_lut_is_a_valid_cube():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        path = look.write_cube(Path(d) / "id.cube", look.bake(lambda x: x, 17), 17)
        lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
    assert lines[1] == "LUT_3D_SIZE 17" and len(lines) == 4 + 17 ** 3
    r, g, b = (float(v) for v in lines[5].split())  # second entry: red varies fastest
    assert r > 0 and g == 0 and b == 0


class FakeFootage:
    """A 30 s clip on the 0.1 s grid with two great moments at 5 s and 20 s."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.N = 300
        t = np.arange(self.N) / 10
        self.interest = np.exp(-((t - 5) ** 2) / 2) + np.exp(-((t - 20) ** 2) / 2)

    def scores(self, L, role, avoid=None):
        c = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(self.interest)])
        out = np.full(self.N, NEG)
        out[: self.N - L + 1] = (c[L:] - c[:-L]) / L
        return out


def test_cutter_keeps_story_order_and_gaps():
    fo = FakeFootage()
    picks = assign_story(fo, [(2.0, "hook"), (2.0, "hold"), (2.0, "hold"), (2.0, "outro")], 0.5)
    starts = [i for i, _ in picks]
    assert starts == sorted(starts)
    for (a, la), (b, _) in zip(picks, picks[1:]):
        assert b >= a + la + 5, "every moment starts after the previous one plus the gap"
    assert any(abs(i / 10 - 4) < 1.5 for i in starts) and any(abs(i / 10 - 19) < 1.5 for i in starts)


def test_rhythm_on_the_beat():
    beats = [round(i * 0.6, 3) for i in range(60)]
    P = {"burst_every": 2, "burst_len": 4, "burst_beats": 1, "outro": 1.5}
    slots = plan_beats(1.2, 14.0, 2.2, P, beats, lambda a, b: 0.8)
    grid = set(round(x, 3) for x in np.concatenate([beats, (np.array(beats[:-1]) + np.array(beats[1:])) / 2]))
    for a, b, _ in slots:
        assert round(a, 3) in grid and round(b, 3) in grid
    assert any(r == "burst" for *_, r in slots) and slots[-1][2] == "outro"
    assert all(abs(b - c) < 1e-6 for (_, b, _), (c, _, _) in zip(slots, slots[1:])), "slots are contiguous"
    free = plan_free(15.0, 2.0, P | {"burst_shot": 0.4})
    assert abs(sum(d for d, _ in free) - 15.0) < 1e-6


def test_type_is_escaped_and_layered():
    st = {"px": 60, "x_px": 540, "y_px": 1200, "y": 0.62, "font": "Montserrat ExtraBold", "color": "F4F1EA",
          "shadow": 0.6, "shade": True}
    doc = ass_document(1080, 1920, [Text(kind="story", text="a {weird} line\\here", start=1, end=3, style=st)])
    events = [ln for ln in doc.splitlines() if ln.startswith("Dialogue:")]
    assert len(events) == 3, "shade band, soft shadow, then the text"
    assert "{weird}" not in doc and "(weird)" in doc
    assert "\\1c&HEAF1F4&" in events[-1]


def test_subject_tracker_follows_a_moving_blob():
    fr = np.full((40, 54, 96, 3), 90, np.uint8)
    for i in range(40):
        x = 20 + i  # a bright, saturated subject moving right
        fr[i, 20:40, x:x + 12] = (200, 60, 50)
    xs, _ = an.subject_track(fr, 8.0)
    assert xs[5] < xs[35] and abs(xs[35] - (55 + 6) / 96) < 0.12


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for name, fn in list(globals().items()):
        if name.startswith("test_") and callable(fn):
            fn()
            print(f"PASS {name}")

input.content:
# Cutroom Studio

**A video editor run by a crew of agents.** Drop raw footage, pick a creative skill (or give it a reference video
to edit like), write the story, and press *Run the line*. Eleven agents, each with one job, hand the edit down an
assembly line: measure the footage, grade it, cut it on the beat, reframe it, move it, set the type, mix the sound,
render it, and check the result.

There is **no model in the edit path**. Every decision is computed from measurements of your footage (FFmpeg decodes,
numpy measures), so the same footage and the same choices always give the same edit, it costs nothing to run, and
every agent can check its own work and say why it did what it did.

![Cutroom Studio](docs/studio.png)

```
uv sync
uv run cutroom studio            # opens http://127.0.0.1:8765
```

Needs FFmpeg 6+ with libass on PATH (`winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` / `brew install ffmpeg` / `apt install ffmpeg`).

> Built for #neatHack 2026: "Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching".

## The line

```
 Intake ─────┐
 Reference ──┼──▶ Colorist ────────────────────────────────┐
 Music ──────┘    Cutter ──▶ Reframer ──▶ Motion ──┬──▶ Typographer ──┬──▶ Export ──▶ QA
                                                   └──▶ Mixer ────────┘        │
                    ▲                                                          │
                    └────────── a failed check goes back to its owner ◀────────┘
```

Agents in the same column work at the same time. An agent whose inputs haven't changed since its last run is
**reused** instead of re-run: change a story line and only the Typographer, Export and QA run again (unchanged
segments aren't even re-rendered).

| Agent | Its one job | What it measures | How it checks itself |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Intake** | probes every clip, makes a light 1080p edit master (1 s keyframes) when the source is 4K or not H.264 | sharpness (Laplacian spread), motion, exposure, clipping, colour, camera cuts (adaptive histogram jumps), where the subject is, sound regions | every clip decodes and is measured end to end |
| **Reference** | watches your reference video *first* | shot-length distribution and bursts, CIELAB colour mean and spread, black/white points, grain, vignette, letterbox, dips to black, tempo and how often its cuts land on the beat | needs at least 3 shots to call it a rhythm |
| **Music** | picks the track and maps it | tempo (onset autocorrelation), beats (dynamic-programming beat tracker), downbeats (kick energy), energy per beat | a clear beat grid, or the cut falls back to the skill's own rhythm |
| **Colorist** | primary correction per clip, shot matching, then the skill's look or the reference's colour, baked into one 3D LUT per clip | levels, mid-grey, saturation and colour cast of each clip | no crushed blacks or blown highlights, a usable mid-grey; when a look crushes a clip it **trims exposure and contrast until its own checks pass**; ΔE to the reference |
| **Cutter** | plans the rhythm and picks a moment for every slot | interest per 0.1 s: sharpness, action, exposure, a clear subject | no cut crosses a camera cut; every cut on a beat when there is music |
| **Reframer** | fits each shot to your format | the subject's position over the shot | subject inside the middle 70% of the frame |
| **Motion** | the skill's moves | which shots hold still, which share a take, the source frame rate, footage beyond each cut | refuses slow motion the frame rate can't make smooth and transitions with no footage beyond the cut |
| **Typographer** | title, time/place stamp, story lines, end card | the graded brightness behind every line | every line placed with time to read it; a soft shade behind any line on a bright background |
| **Mixer** | music from a chosen downbeat, the footage's sound under it, ducking, fades | loudness (EBU R128, two passes) | −14 LUFS ±1, true peak under −1 dBTP |
| **Export** | renders segments in parallel, assembles cuts and transitions, burns in the type | | |
| **QA** | measures the finished file | duration, format, unintended black or frozen frames, loudness, pacing, cuts on the beat, colour distance from the reference | each failure names its owner and a fix; the line re-runs from that agent (up to two rounds) |

### How the cut is made (no model)

1. **Rhythm.** The skill gives a hold length and bursts of quick cuts (bonzo: ~2.2 s holds, a burst of four one-beat
   cuts every two holds). With music, holds snap to whole beats, bursts to beats or half beats, a burst waits until the
   music is loud enough, and the track is entered on the downbeat whose following stretch is loudest.
2. **Moments.** A dynamic program picks one window of footage per slot, maximising the window's score for its role
   (hook: action + sharpness, burst: action, hold: steady interest, outro: calm), in story order, with a gap between
   moments, never across a camera cut.
3. **Moves.** Static holds get a slow push-in; consecutive moments from the same take alternate a punch-in so the jump
   reads as intended; whip pans in and out of bursts (directional blur + slide) where there is footage beyond the cut.

## Skills

A skill is a recipe the agents execute: pacing, colour, moves, type and sound. Pick one, then tune it (pacing, look
strength, grain, music and footage levels, beat sync, transitions, slow motion). The skill gallery shows **your own
footage** in every look.

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| **bonzo** (inspired by @Wordisbonz) | life as a short film: serif title card on black, lowercase time stamp, the story in bold lowercase lines, warm soft film colour with grain and halation, handheld holds broken by whip-pan bursts on the beat |
| **confessional** (inspired by @farzatv) | talk to camera with every pause cut out: jump cuts hidden by alternating punch-ins, natural colour, the voice alone |
| **roaming doc** (inspired by @mayv_music) | handheld documentary: lowercase place stamps, phrase-by-phrase lines, cool muted film colour, rapid hard cuts on the beat |
| **trailer** | 2.39:1 letterbox, teal and orange, slow push-ins, dips to black between acts, spaced capitals on black cards |
| **beat cut** | a cut on every beat or half beat, punch zooms, white flashes into bursts, big words that land on the beat |
| **super 8** | home movie: faded warm stock, heavy grain, gate weave, flicker, an 18 fps cadence, light flashes, a date stamp |
| **dreamy** | a soft memory: dissolves, glowing highlights, pastel colour, slow push-ins, slow motion where the frame rate allows |
| **clean** | balanced colour, unhurried cuts, sentence-case lower thirds |

Only the *style* of the reference creators is used; Cutroom never copies their footage, music or words. Your text is
yours.

### Edit like a reference video

Add a reference and the Reference agent measures it before anything else. With *Edit like the reference* on, its
measured rhythm replaces the skill's (median shot length, how often bursts of short shots happen), the Colorist moves
your footage's colour to the reference's (Reinhard et al.'s mean-and-spread transfer in CIELAB, at the strength you
choose, with grain matched to the reference's measured noise), and its vignette, letterbox and beat sync carry over.
QA then measures the colour distance between your finished video and the reference.

## Why you can walk away from it

- **Deterministic.** Same footage + same choices = the same edit, every time. Nothing is sampled.
- **Every agent checks its own work** and reports its decisions in plain words (click any station in the line).
- **QA measures the actual file** and routes each failure back to the agent that owns it, with a concrete fix.
- **Honest refusals.** No slow motion that would stutter, no transition without footage beyond the cut, no text left
  unreadable on a bright sky. Each refusal is reported.
- **Checkpointed after every agent.** If the process dies, `cutroom rerun <project>` resumes where it stopped; finished
  agents are reused.
- **Traced.** Every agent is a span in [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com) under the `studio.line` workflow (QA is a
  guardrail span); the trace id is in the Report tab.

## What you get

`final.mp4` (H.264 + AAC, Rec.709, −14 LUFS), `poster.jpg`, `edit.edl` (CMX 3600: open the cut in Premiere Pro or
DaVinci Resolve), `edit.json` (the whole edit: timeline, type, sound plan, grade), and the music credit.

## Headless

```
uv run cutroom edit footage/user/clip.mp4 --skill bonzo --title "the coast, again" --stamp "6:42am." \
    --line "i came back for it." --line "the tide moved everything." [--reference ref.mp4] [--aspect 9:16]
uv run cutroom rerun <project-id>      # resume / re-run a studio project
```

Tests: `uv run python tests/test_studio.py` (beat tracking, flat-footage correction, reference colour transfer, LUT
format, story-order cutting, beat-grid rhythm, type escaping, subject tracking).

## Credits

- Music library: Kevin MacLeod ([incompetech.com](https://incompetech.com)), CC BY 4.0. Files are downloaded, not
  committed (see `music/README.md`); the credit is written into every export.
- Fonts: Montserrat, Anton, Bebas Neue, Instrument Serif (SIL Open Font License).
- Demo footage: Blender Foundation open movies (*Tears of Steel*, *Sintel*), CC BY 3.0. See `footage/README.md`.

The repo also contains an earlier experiment (`cutroom make`) in which language models planned the edit. The Studio
replaced it: a measured, deterministic line is faster, free to run, and does what it says.

I scrapped the reel maker and built **Cutroom Studio**: a video editor run by 11 agents, with no AI model making edit decisions. It's running at **http://127.0.0.1:8765**.

**How it works**
- **Your flow:** drop in raw footage, pick a skill, choose the format, write your title, time stamp and story lines, then press *Run the line*. You can add a reference video and it gets measured first, then your footage is edited to match its rhythm, colour, grain and letterbox.
- **The agents:** intake, reference, music, colorist, cutter, reframer, motion, typographer, mixer, export, QA. Each has one job and checks its own work. Agents that don't depend on each other run at the same time. QA measures the finished video and sends any failure back to the agent responsible.
- **Speed on re-runs:** an agent whose inputs didn't change is reused, so editing a story line only re-runs the type, export and QA.
- **Skills:** bonzo (life as a short film), confessional, roaming doc, trailer, beat cut, super 8, dreamy, clean. The skill gallery shows your own footage in each look.
- **The UI:** media bin, viewer with a before/after colour slider, the live assembly line (click any agent to see its decisions and checks), a timeline with beats and transitions, and a report with downloads (MP4, plus an edit list that opens in Premiere or Resolve).

content.text:
**What problem Underwrite solves**

Before an investor puts money into a startup, someone has to answer basic questions:

- Is this company real?
- How much has it raised?
- Who are the founders?
- Is the team growing or shrinking?
- What's in the news?

That research usually takes an analyst **2–4 hours of Googling per company**, and they do it for dozens of companies a week.

Underwrite does it in about **5 minutes** and writes it up as a one-page memo, like the Sequoia memo you showed me.

**Why someone would use it instead of ChatGPT:** ChatGPT can confidently make up numbers. Underwrite checks every fact against a real source and links it. If it can't verify something, it says so. If two sources disagree (the company says 200 employees, the data says 80), it shows you the conflict instead of hiding it. It can also re-check companies every night and tell you when something changes. That's the hackathon theme: an agent you trust without watching.

**Who would use it:**
- Angel investors and VC analysts, before a meeting with a startup.
- Sales teams researching a company before a call.
- Job seekers checking whether a startup is solid before joining.

**Honest weak spots:**
- Paid tools like Crunchbase or Tracxn already give investors raw data. Underwrite's edge is the verified, written memo, not the data itself.
- Investors are a narrow audience, and it's harder for you to demo something you don't personally feel the pain of.

**My suggestion:** the scam-checker idea is basically Underwrite pointed at a problem you and every student know: *"Is this company and this offer real?"* About 70% of the engine is already built (company lookup, web search, fact checking, sources). Reframing it around job and internship offers gives you something you understand and can demo with feeling, and it can realistically be done in the 28 hours left.

Which way do you want to go?
1. **Keep Underwrite as it is** and spend the time on the demo video and posts.
2. **Build the offer scam checker** in a new folder, reusing Underwrite's engine.

Yes, there are competitors, and the space is crowded. Here's the honest picture (from what I know as of mid-2026; I haven't searched live):

**Direct competitors (AI research or due-diligence reports on companies)**
| Who | What they do | Price / who for |
|---|---|---|
| **Wokelo** | AI-written due-diligence and company-research reports | Enterprise, sold to PE/VC firms and consultancies |
| **Hebbia** | AI that reads huge piles of documents for finance teams | Enterprise, big funds and banks |
| **Rogo**, **Brightwave** | "AI analyst" for investors: research and summaries | Enterprise finance teams |
| **AlphaSense** | Market intelligence with AI search over filings, news and expert calls | Expensive, big firms |

**Generic deep-research tools anyone can use**
- ChatGPT Deep Research, Perplexity, Gemini Deep Research. Type a company name and you get a long report.

**Data platforms (raw data, not memos)**
- Crunchbase, PitchBook, Tracxn, CB Insights, Harmonic. They give the numbers; you still write the memo yourself.

**Where Underwrite is different**
1. **It checks every fact.** Each line in the memo is verified against a source. Deep Research tools write fluent reports but can still slip in made-up numbers.
2. **It shows conflicts.** When sources disagree, it tells you instead of picking one quietly.
3. **It keeps watching.** It re-checks companies every night and alerts you only when something actually changed.
4. **It's free and open.** The others cost thousands of dollars a year per seat.

That accuracy drop is exactly what the Coach targeted with its v2 prompt changes. When the eval finishes I'll fill the README results, write the Coach notes, and update the demo script and posts with the real numbers. Good, the site is live. Here's the catch, and the plan:

**The catch:** GitHub Pages can only host fixed pages. It can't run the agent, and it must never hold your API keys. So "use it in the browser" needs a small server that runs Underwrite with your keys, plus limits so strangers can't burn your free credits. Rough capacity: your ~4,800 Crustdata credits ÷ ~10 per memo ≈ 400 memos.

**What I'll build:**
1. **Underwrite Live**, a web app in the same paper-dossier style. Anyone types a company name and website and presses Research. They watch the agents work live (searching, quoting, rejecting bad claims, the skeptic pushing back), then get the full dossier.
   - Companies already researched open instantly.
   - Limits: 2 new memos per visitor per day, a daily cap for the whole site, one job at a time with a queue.
2. **A "Try it live" button** on your current site that opens it.

211	def run_batch(companies: list[tuple[str, str | None]], run_id: str, version: str | None = None,

213	    manifest = settings.runs_dir / run_id / "manifest.json"

222	        left = balance()
223	        low = left is not None and left < settings.min_credit_balance
224	        if low:

229	        if low or spent >= settings.max_credits_per_run:

243	    data = json.loads(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
244	    return run_batch([tuple(x) for x in data["companies"]], run_id, data.get("version"), data.get("mode", "pipeline"))

1	# Running Underwrite unattended on AWS EC2
2	
3	The website on GitHub Pages is static. A small EC2 instance runs the agent every night, adds the new memos to
4	`docs/`, and pushes. Nobody has to be watching: that is the point.
5	
6	**Cost:** a t3.small is about $0.02/hour (~$0.50/day) plus ~$0.05/day for a 20 GB disk. Running it for the whole
7	hackathon and judging week costs a few dollars of the $25 allowance. Stop it when you're done.
8	
9	## 1. Launch the instance (AWS console, logged in with the hackathon IAM user)
10	
11	1. Region **US East (N. Virginia) us-east-1** (top-right).
12	2. EC2 → **Launch instance**:
13	   - Name: `underwrite-runner`
14	   - AMI: **Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS**
15	   - Instance type: **t3.small** (allowed: t2/t3/t3a, nano to large)
16	   - Key pair: create one (`underwrite-key`, .pem) and keep the file private
17	   - Network: **Hackathon_VPC**, any public subnet, **auto-assign public IP: enable**
18	   - Security group: inbound **SSH (22) from My IP only**. Nothing else.
19	   - Storage: 20 GB gp3 (limit is 50 GB)
20	   - No IAM instance profile is needed.
21	3. Launch. Only **one instance per IAM user** is allowed; terminate an old one before launching another.
22

24	
25	EC2 → your instance → **Connect** → **EC2 Instance Connect** → Connect (opens a terminal in the browser). Then:
26	
27	```bash
28	curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hacker-git-code/underwrite-/main/deploy/setup.sh
29	bash setup.sh
30	```
31	
32	The script prints an SSH **public** key. Add it in GitHub → this repo → **Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key**,
33	tick **Allow write access**, save, and press Enter in the terminal. (A deploy key can only push to this one repo.)
34

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Underwrite Live on this EC2 instance: the public web app behind Caddy, with automatic HTTPS.
# Run after setup.sh, as the 'ubuntu' user:   bash ~/underwrite/deploy/web.sh
# The instance's security group must allow inbound HTTP (80) and HTTPS (443) from anywhere.
# No domain needed: the address is <public-ip-with-dashes>.sslip.io (set UW_HOST to use your own domain).
set -euo pipefail

APP="$HOME/underwrite"
IP="$(curl -fsS https://checkip.amazonaws.com | tr -d '[:space:]')"
HOST="${UW_HOST:-${IP//./-}.sslip.io}"
PROMPTS="${UW_PROMPTS:-$(grep -E '^UW_PROMPTS=' "$APP/.env" 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f2 || true)}"
PROMPTS="${PROMPTS:-v1}"

# Caddy: reverse proxy that gets and renews a Let's Encrypt certificate by itself.
if ! command -v caddy >/dev/null; then
  sudo apt-get install -y debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https gnupg
  curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key' | sudo gpg --dearmor --yes -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
  curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list >/dev/null
  sudo apt-get update -y
  sudo apt-get install -y caddy
fi
sudo tee /etc/caddy/Caddyfile >/dev/null <<EOF
$HOST {
	encode gzip
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8080 {
		flush_interval -1
	}
}
EOF
sudo systemctl reload caddy || sudo systemctl restart caddy

# The app as a service: starts on boot, restarts if it crashes; queued jobs resume from their checkpoints.
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/underwrite-web.service >/dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=Underwrite Live
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
User=$USER
WorkingDirectory=$APP
Environment=PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
Environment=UW_PROMPTS=$PROMPTS
ExecStart=$HOME/.local/bin/uv run underwrite serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now underwrite-web
sudo systemctl restart underwrite-web

echo
echo "Underwrite Live is starting at:  https://$HOST"
echo "(the HTTPS certificate takes up to a minute the first time)"
echo "Logs:  journalctl -u underwrite-web -f"
